S01: Many years ago, in a snowy Russian town, lived a rich merchant with his family.
S02: Vasilisa's mother fell ill and lay pale in her chamber.
S03: Knowing her hour was tolling, she called her daughter for a final gift.
S04: When you are in trouble, speak to her. She will help you — the mother whispered to her.
S05: Vasilisa pressed the doll to her breast and quietly wept.
S06: When the mother passed, the house remained empty and silent.
S07: The years passed, and the father remarried a stern woman who brought two spoiled daughters.
S08: The new mistresses looked with contempt at everything around.
S09: All the hardest household work fell upon Vasilisa's shoulders.
S10: The stepmother spared no sharp words for the stepdaughter.
S11: One evening the father announced he was leaving on a long trading journey.
S12: The whole family moved to a house at the very edge of the dark forest.
S13: Of that forest it was whispered that it was the home of the terrible witch Baba Yaga.
S14: Gazing at the forest, Vasilisa clutched the doll like a talisman.
S15: The stepmother, wishing to be rid of Vasilisa, devised a dangerous plan.
S16: The hearth was deliberately extinguished — without spark, without fire.
S17: Stepmother: "Go into the forest and bring fire, while you still can."
S18: Vasilisa seized her doll and, without a word, set out toward the forest.
S19: She sank into the dark forest, among tall trunks that swallowed the moonlight.
S20: Every creak and shadow seemed to her like something lurking.
S21: In her pocket, the doll quietly glowed, urging her onward.
S22: Before her rose Baba Yaga's hut — set upon enormous chicken legs.
S23: Vasilisa stood frozen with fear, and her heart hammered like a smith's.
S24: The walls were of old bone, and the fence — a row of white skulls.
S25: Gathering all her courage, Vasilisa stepped forward and knocked on the door.
S26: The door opened with a creak, and on the threshold stood the witch herself.
S27: Baba Yaga's eyes pierced like sparks.
S28: Vasilisa: "I have come to ask you for a little fire for our home."
S29: Baba Yaga: "I will give you fire, but you must stay and serve me."
S30: Vasilisa nodded and set to work — sweeping, cooking and cleaning.
S31: In secret, the doll helped her — whispering counsel and finishing the hard tasks.
S32: Baba Yaga watched from afar and, satisfied, smiled.
S33: The weeks passed quickly; the hut shone clean and tidy.
S34: Pleased with her conduct, the witch resolved to reward her.
S35: From her breast she drew a staff, and on its tip — a skull with two gleaming diamonds for eyes.
S36: Baba Yaga: "Take it. When you have need, show it — you will receive fire."
S37: With the staff in hand, Vasilisa set out back through the forest — toward home.
S38: When she arrived, at the door awaited her the stepmother and the two stepsisters.
S39: Vasilisa raised the staff high toward the three women.
S40: The skull's eyes flashed so bright that the light vanquished the three women.
S41: Frightened by all that had happened, Vasilisa fled through the night.
S42: She reached the great city, beneath its white towers and golden roofs.
S43: A kind old woman, a skilled seamstress, took her under her roof.
S44: With the doll always beside her, Vasilisa sewed day and night.
S45: Her embroideries grew so fine that all compared them to wonders.
S46: Word of her craft reached even the royal palace.
S47: The tsar marveled at the works and wished to meet the seamstress.
S48: When he saw the beautiful Vasilisa, the tsar fell in love in that very instant.
S49: Soon the splendid wedding was held.
S50: Her father attended, as did the old seamstress... and, of course, the beloved doll.
